source.title: Ruling Out Multi-Order Interference in Quantum Mechanics
source.extraction: Manual extraction checked against PDF text and page images; no raw counts or full PDF retained here.

observable.name: kappa
observable.kappa: epsilon/delta; defined only for nonzero delta

regime: Heralded single photons (HSPS), central interference maximum

alternative_same_summary.relation: Same data summary with different quoted uncertainty; retain discrepancy, do not average or count as independent evidence.

uncertainty_interpretation: Quoted published uncertainty only; no iid Gaussian SEM, total likelihood, significance, confidence interval or acceptance interpretation is assigned.
limitations: Published summary, not raw context counts, covariance or an apparatus likelihood.
Mask displacement can produce illustrative abs(kappa) of order 0.01 (page 7); this is not a rigorous bound or a zero-bias guarantee.
APD counts were kept below 100000 per second to limit dead-time effects; apparatus nuisance bias remains unmodeled.
The meter-only 0.003 systematic estimate is not assigned to the HSPS result.
Historical-source selection is not prospective preregistration.

The null is a fixed-path algebra identity, not an exact universal apparatus prediction for actual triple slits. Slit switching changes boundary conditions; nonclassical paths can give nonzero kappa within ordinary QM. Source: Sawant et al., Non-classical paths in interference experiments, https://arxiv.org/html/1308.2022v2. Its Imax normalization is not imported into this Sinha sum-of-pair-interference comparison; no numerical correction is applied.
